title: Read the Routing Table
subtitle: Category to queue, as config
scenario: Routing is a lookup, not a judgement. Read Relay's routing table - the governed map from category to its destination queue - and record it. Queue names come only from this table, so a ticket is never sent to a queue that does not exist.
input:
Relay's routing table (owned by the Queue Lead) maps each category to its standard queue:
outage -> incident-bridge
bug -> bug-queue
how-to -> support-queue
billing -> billing-queue
(P1 tickets escalate regardless of queue - that is the route decision's job.) Record the category-to-queue mapping.
instructions: Record each category's standard queue from the table.
Use queue names exactly as the table lists them.
Return a JSON array of the four rows, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Record the routing table as a JSON array: one row per category (outage, bug, how-to, billing) with its standard queue. Use the exact queue names.
successMessage: Routing table recorded. The route decision now maps each ticket to a real queue.
editorHelper: One row per category - queue names come only from here.

sections.title: Routing is a lookup
sections.body: Given a category (and priority), the destination queue is a table lookup, not a per-ticket decision. Config-as-rules is what keeps routing consistent across a whole desk.

sections.title: Queues come from the table
sections.body: A ticket can only go to a queue the table names. That constraint is what prevents tickets vanishing into a mistyped or non-existent queue.

sections.title: Owned by the Queue Lead
sections.body: The Queue Lead owns the routing table. When queues are added or retired, the table changes once and every ticket follows - no agent re-learning where things go.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A routing-table record the route decision applies, with P1 escalation layered on top.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd keep a category-to-queue table and route every ticket by looking it up, not by remembering where each kind goes.

tools.powerAutomate: a lookup list of category -> queue
